title: Famous inventors and the country they were born in

source.name: Wikidata (CC0)
source.method: sparql:SELECT ?item ?itemLabel ?article ?sitelinks ?countryLabel WHERE { { SELECT ?item (SAMPLE(?c) AS ?country) (COUNT(DISTINCT ?c) AS ?nC) WHERE { ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q5 ; wdt:P106 wd:Q205375 ; wdt:P19 ?bp . ?bp wdt:P17 ?c . ?item wikibase:sitelinks ?s . FILTER(?s >= 30) } GROUP BY ?item } hint:Prior hint:runFirst true . FILTER(?nC = 1) OPTIONAL { ?article schema:about ?item ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> . } ?item wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks . SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en,mul". } } ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks) LIMIT 160

country.match: Match each inventor to the country they were born in.
country.odd: Three of these inventors were born in {value}. Which one was not?
country.reverse: Which of these inventors was born in {value}?

rows.label: Steve Jobs
rows.description: American entrepreneur; co-founder of Apple Inc. (1955–2011)
rows.hook: co-founded the computer company behind the iPhone and Mac

rows.label: Nikola Tesla
rows.hook: championed alternating current power and the induction motor

rows.label: Steve Wozniak
rows.description: American computer pioneer, inventor, computer engineer and programmer; co-founder of Apple Inc.
rows.hook: designed the first Apple computers as the engineer of a famous garage duo

rows.label: Hedy Lamarr
rows.description: Austrian-American actress and co-inventor of an early technique for spread spectrum communications and frequency hopping (1914-2000)
rows.hook: was a Hollywood star who co-invented frequency hopping, a forerunner of Wi-Fi and Bluetooth tech

rows.label: Thomas Edison
rows.hook: developed a practical light bulb and the phonograph

rows.label: Ada Lovelace
rows.hook: is often called the first computer programmer for her notes on an early mechanical computer

rows.label: Henry Ford
rows.hook: made cars affordable to ordinary families with the moving assembly line

rows.label: Alexander Graham Bell
rows.hook: patented the first practical telephone

rows.label: Linus Torvalds
rows.hook: created the Linux kernel as a student and gave it away for free

rows.label: Tim Berners-Lee
rows.hook: invented the World Wide Web

rows.label: Michael Faraday
rows.hook: discovered electromagnetic induction and laid the groundwork for electric motors and generators

rows.label: George Washington Carver
rows.hook: is famed for promoting hundreds of uses for peanuts and better crop rotation

rows.label: Charles Babbage
rows.hook: designed the Difference Engine, an early mechanical computer

rows.label: Alexander Fleming
rows.description: Scottish biologist, pharmacologist, botanist, and Nobel laureate (1881–1955)
rows.hook: discovered penicillin after noticing mould killing bacteria on a lab dish

rows.label: Johannes Gutenberg
rows.hook: introduced the movable-type printing press to Europe

rows.label: Guglielmo Marconi
rows.hook: pioneered long-distance radio transmission and wireless telegraphy

rows.label: Ferdinand Porsche
rows.hook: designed the original Volkswagen Beetle and founded a famous sports car brand

rows.label: Jonas Salk
rows.hook: developed the first widely used polio vaccine

rows.label: Les Paul
rows.description: American jazz guitarist, country guitarist, songwriter and inventor (1915–2009)
rows.hook: pioneered multitrack recording and helped design a famous solid-body electric guitar bearing his name

rows.label: Richard Stallman
rows.description: American software freedom activist, short story writer and computer programmer, founder of the GNU project
rows.hook: founded the GNU project and the free software movement

rows.label: Robert Hooke
rows.description: English natural philosopher, architect and polymath (1635 — 1703)
rows.hook: coined the biological term cell after studying cork under a microscope

rows.label: Carl Benz
rows.description: German automotive and engine designer and manufacturer (1844–1929)
rows.hook: built the first practical gasoline-powered automobile

rows.label: Buckminster Fuller
rows.description: American architect, systems theorist, author, designer, inventor and futurist (1895–1983)
rows.hook: popularized the geodesic dome

rows.label: James Watt
rows.hook: greatly improved the steam engine, helping to power the Industrial Revolution

rows.label: Rudolf Diesel
rows.hook: invented an engine that ignites its fuel by compression alone

rows.label: William Shockley
rows.hook: co-invented the transistor, helping give rise to Silicon Valley

rows.label: Alessandro Volta
rows.hook: built the first electric battery, the voltaic pile

rows.label: Igor Sikorsky
rows.description: American aviation pioneer from Russian Empire (1889–1972)
rows.hook: built the first mass-produced helicopter

rows.label: Samuel Finley Breese Morse
rows.hook: developed the electric telegraph and a dot-and-dash code to go with it

rows.label: Louis Braille
rows.description: French organist and teacher (1809-1852), inventor of braille, a system for reading and writing text and music, used by people who are blind or visually impaired
rows.hook: created a raised-dot reading and writing system for blind people

rows.label: Christiaan Huygens
rows.hook: invented the pendulum clock and discovered Saturn's largest moon

rows.label: Robert H. Goddard
rows.hook: launched the world's first liquid-fueled rocket

rows.label: John Logie Baird
rows.description: Scottish inventor, demonstrating the world's first working television (1888–1946)
rows.hook: gave the first public demonstration of a working television
